## 2. Copy framing

The Wegovy Backed Me Up. MiraLax, Fiber, a $600 Script - None Fixed Why.

I'm a nurse. 38 years. So when the constipation from my Wegovy got bad, I tried to fix it the way I'd fix anything. One careful step at a time.

MiraLax first. Then the fiber powder everyone swears by, that gritty sludge you choke down twice a day. When those stopped touching it, my own doctor slid a $600-a-month script for Linzess across the desk like it settled things.

Here's the part nobody tells you. Every one of those options was built to force something out. Not one fixed why my gut had quit in the first place. And each came with its own misery. I'd watched Linzess patients so scared of the diarrhea they couldn't be 30 seconds from a bathroom. One took time off work over it.

I didn't want a chemical evacuation on a timer. I wanted my own body working again, the way it had my whole life.

Quitting the shot was never on the table. Go off it and the weight comes back. I'd watched too many patients do exactly that. Square one.

So I stayed backed up. Seven, eight, nine days of nothing. Bloated like I'd swallowed rocks, and scared of where it was heading.

I've been a nurse too long to chase every fix that gets passed around online. I'd about made my peace that this was just my life now.

Then about two months ago, one of my regular patients came in for her appointment. Sweet lady on Mounjaro for the past few months. She'd been struggling with constipation the entire time - two months of living off laxatives, miserable.

But this time she seemed different. More relaxed somehow.

I asked her how she was managing, and she said something I didn't expect. She told me she was actually going regularly now. She'd found this tea - oolong tea - with natural antioxidants and gentle caffeine. Been drinking it every morning. And for the first time in months, she was having normal bowel movements. No cramping. No laxatives. No fear.

I'll be honest, I was very skeptical. I've heard every miracle cure story you can imagine. But she seemed so genuinely relieved. Like she'd finally found something that actually worked.

That same night, I was on day 8 without a bowel movement. My stomach was so distended I couldn't sleep comfortably. I laid there feeling bloated and genuinely scared. And I kept thinking about what she'd said. So I looked it up.

Turns out, the antioxidants in oolong tea - along with natural caffeine and L-theanine - support digestive motility and gut microbiome health naturally. It doesn't force contractions like stimulant laxatives do. Plus it hydrates you and activates your body's natural gastrocolic reflex. The science actually made sense.

I ordered some. Figured I had nothing to lose. Worst case, it wouldn't work and I'd be out a few dollars.

When it arrived, I made a cup that first morning. I didn't expect much. Just another thing to try.

After about a week, things started moving a little. From once a week to every 4-5 days. Better. But not life-changing.

So I ordered a different brand. This one was cheaper, came in tea bags instead of loose leaf. After two weeks, things stayed about the same. Maybe every 3-4 days. Still too uncomfortable.

I was getting frustrated. Everyone said oolong tea worked. But it wasn't working for me.

So I went back and started reading more carefully. That's when I noticed something. People weren't just saying "oolong tea." They were getting specific about which oolong tea.

One person said they tried three different brands before finding one that actually worked. Another mentioned most oolong tea you can buy online is "tea dust" - the broken leftover scraps from processing that don't have any of the actual healing compounds.

I started researching. Turns out, most oolong teas are:

\- Over-processed (which destroys the polyphenols)

\- Grown at low elevations (weaker potency)

\- Mixed with tea dust and fillers

\- Sprayed with pesticides

\- Machine-harvested (damages the leaves)

The oolong teas that actually worked for digestive support had to be:

\- Whole leaf (not dust or broken pieces)

\- Grown above 4,500 feet (higher altitude = more potent polyphenols)

\- Hand-picked at peak harvest (preserves the catechins and L-theanine)

\- Traditionally processed (protects the healing compounds)

\- Organic (no pesticides blocking absorption)

I kept seeing the same brand mentioned over and over in the reviews and testimonials. PiPi Tea.

I ordered it. It was more expensive than the others I'd tried, but at that point I didn't care.

When it arrived, I could tell the difference immediately. The leaves were whole, tightly rolled, and perfectly oxidized. The smell was different - richer, almost floral. When I steeped it, the color was deeper.

I made a cup that first morning. Steeped it for five minutes. I didn't expect much. I'd already tried two other brands.

But about 30 minutes later, I noticed something. The usual morning bloat wasn't building up. Like someone had activated my digestive system again. I went from feeling that constant pressure in my abdomen to actually feeling movement - gentle, natural movement. I could actually feel the gastrocolic reflex working like it should for the first time in months.

That night, I had my first normal bowel movement in over a week. Actually normal - no straining. No cramping. No sitting there for 30 minutes with nothing happening. Just... normal.

When I woke up the next morning, I laid there stunned. The bloated feeling was gone. I'd slept through the night without that rock-in-my-stomach feeling for the first time in months.

By the end of the first week, I was going every single day. Every day. Not every 4-5 days like with the other brands. Every single morning like clockwork. I tracked it for three days straight because I didn't believe it. It hadn't been regular in months.

That bloated feeling that made me afraid to eat? Gone. The straining for hours with nothing happening? Cleared up almost completely. I could work a full shift without feeling backed up and uncomfortable.

It's been two months now. I go every single morning. Every morning. The bloating is gone. The fear is gone. Sometimes I skip a day after a really stressful shift when I'm not drinking enough water, but it's nothing. Nothing compared to what it was.

I saw my patient last week and thanked her. She just smiled and said she was glad it helped.

Look, for months I thought I just had to live with the bloating and backed-up feeling. That this was my life now. But I was wrong.

And here's the thing - not all oolong tea is created equal. I wasted weeks on cheap brands that barely moved the needle. PiPi Tea's organic, high-altitude, whole-leaf oolong is the only one that actually worked.

If my patient hadn't mentioned oolong tea that day, I'd still be backed up, bloated, and afraid to eat.

I've told five of my patients on GLP-1s about PiPi Tea's oolong specifically. Every single one of them has come back and said they're finally regular again. One lady told me she's going daily for the first time since starting Ozempic - three months ago.

I'm sharing this because I hope it can help someone else the way it helped me. After 38 years as a nurse, I thought I knew every option out there. Turns out, my patient knew something I didn't.

Here's where I got mine: https://shop.pipitea.com/p/sp

(They're running a sale right now, significant savings. I just ordered 3 more bags)

~ Sandra K.

P.S. - A few things I wish I'd known before ordering:

When I first ordered PiPi Tea, I didn't know they had a 90-day money-back guarantee. If it doesn't work for you, you get your money back. No questions asked. I wish I'd known that earlier - would've saved me from trying those cheaper brands that didn't do anything.

Most people buy it at regular price, but right now they're running a promotion where you can get it at a significant discount. That's actually how I was able to stock up on three bags - the savings made it possible.

The only problem is that PiPi Tea is a small, family-run company. They're getting really popular (probably because nurses like me keep recommending it to patients), and they can't always keep up with demand.

I want to apologize in advance because when you click the link below, you might see that they're sold out. I've had patients wait months before PiPi Tea was back in stock. But I'd still suggest clicking to see if they have any left.

If you're dealing with GLP-1 constipation, bloating, backed-up feeling, or fear of eating - and especially if laxatives are making your life miserable - I'd grab some before they're gone again.

I went from once a week to every single morning in three months. If there's even a chance this could work for you, it's worth trying.

Natural Relief in Weeks
